acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE FIRST RULE IN THIS PRODUCT WITH A JOB. Before it, core/lwb_core/rules/ held one rule whose own docstring calls it a safe no-op that never denies, and a consuming repo that installed lwb got exactly that

PURITY HELD, which was the design risk: the rule performs no I/O. The impure adapter collects branch and proof ids into a declared RepoFacts field; the pure rule decides from those alone. The reviewer proved it by BLOCKING open, os file and process calls, subprocess, socket and pathlib reads so they would raise, then running the rule's tests -- 35 passed

It honours config.mode, unlike lwb_version which hardcodes WARN: warn permits with a WARN finding, deny returns permit=False, off is silent, deny with a matching record permits. The first time anything in this product has denied anything
EXERCISED OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY, through the shipped bin/lwb_hook.py against a genuinely foreign git repo -- the first time any of this product has run anywhere but here

BLOCKER FIXED: a branch name containing a slash can now be cleared. The rule names proof/feat/x-12.json, creating exactly that path silences it -- verified end to end in a foreign repo on branch feat/x-12. Ids use forward slashes on every platform, so Windows does not reproduce the bug natively

Two parser under-matches fixed and reproduced first: a heredoc introducer inside quotes, and <<< treated as a heredoc when it is a herestring. All 20 parser cases behave -- 9 true negatives silent, 5 true positives caught, both fixes, and the gh-pr-create case

NO SHIPPED POLICY ARMS THE RULE TO DENY, and the lock covers the VENDORED copies that actually ship rather than only the source policy. Proved non-vacuous: arming a vendored policy makes the test fail
hooks.json gains a Bash matcher and keeps Agent. Bash is the matcher that makes the rule run; Agent has never been observed to fire

unproven: DENY IS ADVISORY, NOT A SECURITY CONTROL, and the doc says so in those words. The reviewer CONFIRMED that a bare repo, a missing .git, a corrupt HEAD and a detached HEAD all permit under deny -- the first two because event.repo is None, the latter two because RepoFacts(branch=None). Detaching HEAD in one call and pushing in the next defeats deny entirely. Also undetected: git -C <path> push, (git push), command git push, FOO=1 git push, echo $(git push), git.exe push, and a push inside an invoked script. Making deny fail CLOSED on missing facts is what it would take, and that is NOT done here.

repo=None MEANS SILENCE, deliberately and not fixed. Making it fail closed at warn would fire in every directory without a .git, which is worse than the gap. This is the same fail-open shape as the gh-unauthenticated path that hid the #24 bug from CI for its entire life, and it is chosen with that precedent in view rather than in ignorance of it.

THE RULE IS INERT ON CODEX: adapters/codex/hook_io.py supplies no RepoFacts, so Event.repo is None on every Codex event. The protocol is enforced on one host today. Not fixed because adapters/codex/ is not this author's lane.
WRONG-REPOSITORY EXPOSURE, PLAUSIBLE, NOT REPRODUCED: facts come from the session's cwd, so 'cd ../other && git push' is judged against the session repo's branch. Reviewer finding 4.

NOT CHECKED BY THE REVIEWER: a symlinked .git, PowerShell-native invocation forms beyond '& git push', and the end-to-end bin/lwb_hook.py run driven from hooks.json. The author ran bin/lwb_hook.py directly against a foreign repo, which is not the same as the hook being invoked BY Claude Code from hooks.json -- that path has still never been observed to fire.
THE 'Agent' MATCHER REMAINS UNCONFIRMED. Bash was added precisely because Agent has never been seen to fire; keeping Agent costs nothing but proves nothing.
